description: GTFS Segments is a Python library for measuring bus-stop spacing from General Transit Feed Specification schedules. It reads stops and route shapes, snaps stops onto routes, splits routes into the segments between consecutive stops, and returns a GeoDataFrame. The package can compute spacing summaries weighted by service frequency, make histograms or maps, and export segment data as CSV or GeoJSON. It also reports route measures such as length, headway and speed. Its spatial extent and service period follow the feed supplied by the user; it is not a fixed bus-network dataset. Public repository metadata and package documentation show MIT source access. The outputs can help compare bus stop placement, prepare a service-network representation, or set stop-spacing parameters for public-transport simulation. Snapping and route geometry depend on feed completeness and accuracy, so maps and summaries should be checked against the original schedule. The related catalogue record data-gtfs-specification describes the input standard, not this processing library. This review read the JOSS article and source documentation, but did not fetch feeds or execute the software.
